episode_title: Sam Roberts: COOK, YOUNG and KEIDAN: cyklaw

real_qa.q: What are the main types of fintech disputes that law firms handle?
real_qa.r: Fintech disputes fall into several buckets: disputes directly about the technology itself, such as software licensing disagreements between fintechs and institutions over upgrades or installation rights; disputes where software is incidental, such as M&A warranty breaches when a buyer discovers the acquired fintech business is not what was represented; and fraud-related disputes, such as theft of crypto assets using technology.

real_qa.q: What warranties should fintech sellers include in M&A sale agreements?
real_qa.r: Sellers typically give warranties covering financial performance in the years leading up to sale, business warranties such as data protection compliance and staff training, and warranties specific to core technology stating that software does what it is supposed to do with no known vulnerabilities or bugs. If any warranty proves untrue, the buyer may claim breach of warranty and seek reimbursement for the difference in value.

real_qa.q: What disclosure and carve-outs should fintech founders provide in acquisition agreements?
real_qa.r: Founders should provide disclosure of any known issues or investigations that might otherwise be covered by warranties—for example, a regulatory letter asking questions about the business. Anything given in disclosure is carved out from the warranties, so sellers must be extremely careful about what they disclose because it signals what they are explicitly acknowledging as potential issues.

real_qa.q: Why do fintech founders need legal counsel before selling their company?
real_qa.r: Young fintech founders often possess strong technical and product skills but lack legal and contractual expertise, leaving them vulnerable during M&A negotiations. A commercial lawyer is essential to negotiate sale agreements, ensure accuracy of warranties, and structure disclosure properly to avoid liability for breach of warranty claims—which can be brought for reasons unrelated to actual business performance if the acquiring company encounters cash issues.
real_qa.requete: fintech founder legal advice M&A acquisition

real_qa.q: How can fintech acquirers use breach of warranty claims opportunistically?
real_qa.r: After acquiring a fintech, larger companies may look to 'kick the tires' months later and, even if unrelated parts of the parent company are underperforming or facing cash issues, seek breach of warranty claims against the seller as an obvious source of recovery—sometimes even when claims are not entirely in good faith—making it critical for sellers to have documentation and disclosure in order from the outset.

guest.bio_context: Sam Roberts is a partner at CYK Commercial, a conflict-free disputes-only boutique law firm based in the City of London, established in January 2009 at the end of the financial crisis. He has spent years cutting his teeth on financial services disputes ranging from loans and mortgages to exotic financial derivatives, which comprised 75-80% of the firm's early work. His personal focus has long centered on technology, culminating in a specialization in fintech disputes where financial services expertise and technology interest converge.
